analysis.headline: A Chinese broker based in Honduras gets 12 years in a US cocaine, laundering and terrorism-support case
analysis.what_happened: Wenshen Xu, a Honduras-based Chinese national extradited from Guatemala, received 12 years in prison, the Justice Department says. In Oaxaca, three travellers from Dallas were caught with 365,865 undeclared dollars, Borderland Beat reports.
analysis.says_vs_does: A Democratic senator asked for a full probe of Bank of America, and La Opinión says a fifth of the sum is tied to Chinese networks and cartels. That is an allegation, not a proven laundering finding.
analysis.follow_the_money: Xu received a 22 million dollar money judgement. The Oaxaca seizure was 365,865 dollars and 5,900 pesos moving south from Texas.
analysis.at_stake: US prosecutors show Chinese brokers in Central America within reach of terrorism charges. Smugglers lost bulk cash at a regional airport rather than a land crossing.
tensions: Chinese money brokers vs US prosecutors: the FTO designations now reach launderers as well as traffickers.

analysis.headline: Costa Rican prosecutors say cargo-theft gangs load drugs into legitimate containers as Panama seizes 1,208 packages
analysis.what_happened: Costa Rica's prosecutors found that gangs combining cargo theft, extortion and drug trafficking use customs information to pick high-value loads, Infobae reports. Panama seized 1,208 drug packages in under 24 hours, including in Chilean goods bound for Spain.
analysis.says_vs_does: The Costa Rican state itself calls its response insufficient, Infobae reports. Trucking firms report three hijackings a week in 2025.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: Gangs gain access to legitimate export chains through customs data. Exporters face contaminated containers they did not load.
tensions: Cargo gangs vs Costa Rican customs: the gangs exploit the state's own shipping data.

analysis.what_happened: Texas authorised its National Guard to enter nine islands in the Rio Grande for border security, El País reports. Mexico's foreign ministry asked that boundary treaties be respected and called it a federal matter.
analysis.says_vs_does: Texas frames the move as operational security. WOLA notes CBP has not published last month's apprehension and seizure data, so official border claims lack their usual public record.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: Texas asserts control over disputed river land on its own authority. Mexico defends treaty boundaries without confronting the US federal government.
tensions: Texas vs Mexico: a state government acts on land the two countries manage by treaty.

analysis.says_vs_does: Authorities call him the CJNG plaza boss for Veracruz-Boca del Río and El Tanque's direct successor. That label is an official claim; corridos cited by Milenio and Infobae celebrated his rise before any charge.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: The federal government shows a second blow to the same CJNG regional command within a month, after El Tanque's arrest on 5 October. The CJNG loses another Gulf-coast manager during its succession.
tensions: Federal forces vs CJNG Gulf command: two successive regional chiefs have fallen since 5 October.

analysis.headline: Colombian police and the FBI arrest two Mexicans described as the CJNG's main links to the Clan del Golfo
analysis.what_happened: Colombia's National Police and the FBI arrested two Mexican nationals, alias La Patrona and La Pau, in Barranquilla on 28 October, El Tiempo and Proceso report. They are held for extradition to the United States.
analysis.says_vs_does: Police describe them as the two main links between the CJNG and the Clan del Golfo for large cocaine shipments. Sources show no charging documents yet, so the role rests on police statements.

analysis.at_stake: The arrests target the supplier relationship between Colombia's largest armed group and a Mexican buyer, not street distribution. The CJNG loses brokers at the point where cocaine changes hands.
tensions: CJNG and Clan del Golfo vs joint US-Colombian enforcement: the arrests hit the wholesale link between producer and buyer.

analysis.what_happened: President Sheinbaum said homicides in Sinaloa have risen in recent days and that she sent the Security Cabinet to the state, La Jornada and Milenio report. Milenio counted at least 13 dead in one day.
analysis.says_vs_does: Sheinbaum says intelligence analysis has been done to explain the rise. The visible response is supervision visits by Trevilla in Mazatlán and García Harfuch at Culiacán's C4i, not a new announced operation.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: The federal government seeks to show control over a war now past two years. A house reportedly used as Governor Rocha Moya's campaign office was shot at on 26 October in Culiacán.
tensions: Chapitos vs Mayiza: the homicide rise follows the killing of Chuy González and arrests in the Chapitos arms network.

analysis.says_vs_does: De la Espriella announced the strike in advance and called it very important and strategic. Outlets disagree on the target: Caracol places it in Chocó against the Clan del Golfo, while one El Tiempo report names Mordisco's dissidents.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: The president gains a show of force after loosening some restrictions on bombings, Yahoo Noticias reports. La FM reports that an earlier bombing in his term killed four dissidents, including a 16-year-old.
tensions: Colombian state vs Clan del Golfo and FARC dissidents: air strikes have returned as a routine tool under the new government.

analysis.headline: Rio police target a Comando Vermelho gas-cylinder monopoly as Mato Grosso do Sul arrests PCC and CV members
analysis.what_happened: Operação Dominus targeted a Comando Vermelho group in Rio de Janeiro that imposed a monopoly on cooking gas, G1 reports. In Mato Grosso do Sul, police served 20 arrest warrants over the PCC-CV dispute.
analysis.says_vs_does: The record shows the CV acting as a tax and market authority in areas it controls, forcing traders to meet sales targets. This goes beyond drug trafficking into control of household goods.
analysis.follow_the_money: The group charged 150 reais per gas cylinder and set sales quotas for merchants, G1 reports. Sources do not give a total revenue figure.
analysis.at_stake: The CV draws steady income from residents regardless of drug markets. Brazilian police seek to cut that revenue, while the PCC and CV compete for territory in Mato Grosso do Sul.
tensions: PCC vs Comando Vermelho: the MS investigation identified 22 people involved in the two factions' dispute.

analysis.headline: US charges 24 in a Sinaloa-linked Tennessee network run from state prisons, as CBP reports large port seizures
analysis.what_happened: US prosecutors charged 24 members of a network linked to the Sinaloa Cartel that distributed meth, fentanyl and cocaine in Tennessee, Infobae reports. CBP seized nearly 1,600 pounds of meth at Otay Mesa.
analysis.says_vs_does: US authorities link the Tennessee network to the Sinaloa Cartel. Sources name no faction, and two leaders allegedly ran it from state prisons, which points to local control.
analysis.follow_the_money: CBP valued the Otay Mesa meth at 2.5 million dollars and a Brownsville cocaine load at 611,000 dollars. Seizure values are agency estimates and measure enforcement as well as traffic.
analysis.at_stake: US prosecutors show reach into retail distribution. Commercial trucks at ports of entry remain the documented crossing method in these cases.
tensions: US enforcement vs cartel supply: seizures concentrate at commercial crossings in California and Texas.

analysis.follow_the_money: The US offered a reward of 5 million dollars. Expansión reports that US authorities linked him in May to drug trafficking and laundering for the Sinaloa Cartel; sources do not give laundering figures.
analysis.at_stake: Mexico gains a high-value result on a US most-wanted target before federal security chiefs tour Sinaloa. His network's northern Sinaloa heroin and fentanyl production loses a senior manager.
tensions: Chapitos vs Mayiza: outlets disagree on which faction González Peñuelas served when he died.

analysis.what_happened: Chihuahua Governor Maru Campos told Carlos Loret that Morena leader Ariadna Montiel has ties to organised crime, citing a meeting involving El Guano. The federal Security Cabinet denied the meeting and any intelligence report.
analysis.says_vs_does: Both sides offer claims, not evidence. Campos has shown no documents in sources, and the federal denial came by social-media message; Montiel is preparing three legal complaints against Campos.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: Campos gains a national platform against Morena in a state contested by Sinaloa factions. Montiel and the federal government seek to contain a narco-politics charge against the ruling party.
